## 1. Prediction market

On [Polymarket](https://polymarket.com/event/brazil-presidential-election), the presidential reading reinforced Lula's favoritism: the PT candidate rose to 47.50% (USD 6.38M accumulated), a gain of around 3.00pp in 48 hours, while Flávio Bolsonaro fell to 26.50% (USD 6.58M), a decline of 1.50pp. The gap between the two widened to +21.00pp, the largest of the cycle and well above the +10pp difference measured in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) of Genial/[Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest) on June 10. Renan Santos retreated to 13.70% (USD 6.93M) in the winner market, a drop of 2.00pp. The presidential market has accumulated a total volume of approximately USD 99.04M traded since opening, reinforcing the weight of real money behind the prices.

In the third way, the [base remained compressed in the market](https://polymarket.com/event/brazil-presidential-election): Camilo Santana at 2.80% (USD 3.29M), Fernando Haddad at 1.90% (USD 5.69M), Ronaldo Caiado at 1.60% (USD 4.00M) and Romeu Zema at 1.20% (USD 3.59M), all without traction in the bipolarized Lula × Flávio dispute dominating the cycle.

In the [market for second place in the first round](https://polymarket.com/event/brazil-presidential-election), Flávio maintained isolated leadership at 66.50%, with Renan at 16.50%. In the market for third place in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno), Renan remained isolated favorite at 51.50%, ahead of Zema (19.00%) and Caiado (16.50%), a contrast with his decline in the winner market.

In the [institutional and macro sub-markets](https://polymarket.com/event/brazil-presidential-election), the impeachment contract for [STF](/en/glossary#stf) minister before 2027 remained stable at 2.30% (low volume, USD ~80k), reflecting the de-escalation of the Master case. In the Senate, [PL](/en/glossary#pl) led the race for more seats at 72.50% (USD 243k). In the annual inflation market for 2026, the 5.50% to 6.00% range led at 26.50%, followed closely by the 5.00% to 5.50% range (26.20%).

## 2. What the institutes recorded

No new Tier 1 national poll was published on June 12. The Genial/[Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest) poll from June 10 (n=2.004, field from June 5–8, 2pp margin) remained the most recent national snapshot, with Lula at 39% and Flávio at 29% in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) (gap +10pp) and Lula at 44% versus 38% in the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) (gap +6pp), [winning all scenarios](https://news.google.?oc=5). Earlier open-access polls, such as the Alfa released by Exame, reinforced the PT candidate's advantage (Lula 40% × Flávio 31% in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno)).

The data that gained traction during the day was a breakdown from [Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest) itself: among evangelicals, Flávio fell from 61% to 52% (−9pp) and Lula rose from 24% to 31% (+7pp), while among Catholics the senator remained stable (34%), according to [Brasil 247](https://www.brasil247.com/brasil/flavio-bolsonaro-perde-apoio-entre-evangelicos-aponta-quaest) and [CartaCapital](https://www.cartacapital.com.br/cartaexpressa/as-intencoes-de-voto-para-presidente-entre-evangelicos-e-catolicos-segundo-a-quaest/). The movement was flagged by the press as the main driver of Flávio's loss of competitiveness in the aggregate.

## 3. What the press covered

In the opposition, the religious reading from [Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest) dominated coverage: [Mônica Bergamo, in Folha de S.Paulo](https://news.google.?oc=5), and other outlets highlighted Flávio's decline among evangelicals, with [Revista Fórum](https://revistaforum.com.br/politica/queda-evangelicos-pesadelo-flavio-bolsonaro/) treating the segment as a campaign concern. On the symbolic front, Flávio asked voters to [wear "the Bolsonaro shirt"](https://news.google.?oc=5) to cheer for the national team, an episode that fueled the narrative power struggle with the government. The reading that [evangelicals were responsible for the decline](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiUkFVX3lxTE5reEU3ODEwbW1WNmczclUtZG1HMl9qMVpxZXY4WEx2ZXRYZDd5UkhwZFo4Y3pJWU1PdTY4ZmZYMWtOMW1QLVhTdUQ0ajZKSnl5THc?oc=5) circulated among secondary candidates.

On the government side, coverage was contradictory: while the market priced stronger favoritism for Lula, news reports registered fronts of wear. [Estadão](https://news.google.?oc=5) covered David Alcolumbre's strategy in the Senate, and Folha de S.Paulo reported that the [government seeks an agreement with the Senate president](https://news.google.?oc=5) to avoid wear on the security agenda and among evangelicals, amid pressure from the so-called 6x1.

On the institutional agenda, the [INSS](/en/glossary#inss) fraud case returned to center stage: Folha de S.Paulo reported that the [INSS promoted an employee who authorized agreements for illegal discounts](https://www1.folha.uol.com.br/colunas/painel/2026/06/inss-promove-servidora-que-autorizou-acordos-para-descontos-ilegais-de-aposentados.shtml) on pensions, and the [Court of Audit created a new perquisite for civil servants](https://www1.folha.uol.com.br/poder/2026/06/tcu-cria-novo-penduricalho-para-servidores-apos-ver-brecha-em-decisao-do-stf.shtml) after finding a loophole in an [STF](/en/glossary#stf) ruling. On the credibility front, the [attempted concealment of documents on sports betting](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMilgFBVV95cUxPMWc0ejNqMXd4TUdkMWpHc1RfRW42eXEwVGxFT0QyU29FRmx0M1NjbzVJMDBiTWxqbGFKOFBhc1BBbmJHVHMteF9vb1JiSWpac09sMy1NYldISUZDN1VJN3pGYjJmUjZ5ZnFwTjBXWXliZEo4WW9UNGxBYkhlaE5USVNzSnRER3VIRVp5RG5VQl9MRnktSUE?oc=5) was treated as a new crisis for the government. The Master/Vorcaro case, in turn, lost momentum in the day's news coverage, in line with the [STF](/en/glossary#stf) impeachment contract stalled at 2.30%.

## 4. Divergences of the day

> **Market × survey (widest gap):** Renan Santos appears at 13.70% in the [winner market](https://polymarket.com/event/brazil-presidential-election), versus 3% in [Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest)'s [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) of June 10 — a divergence of approximately 10.70pp, the largest on the dashboard. The market, however, maintains him as the isolated favorite for 3rd place in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) (51.50%), which suggests that the bet is less about victory and more about the podium.

> **Market × survey (presidential gap):** Lula's gap over Flávio in the [winner market](https://polymarket.com/event/brazil-presidential-election) widened to +21.00pp, double the +10pp gap measured in [Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest)'s [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) and well above the +6pp of the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno). The market prices a stronger favoritism than surveys declare.

> **Market × narrative:** while the news accumulated damage fronts for the government (6x1, bets, [INSS/TCU](https://www1.folha.uol.com.br/poder/2026/06/tcu-cria-novo-penduricalho-para-servidores-apos-ver-brecha-em-decisao-do-stf.shtml)), Lula's contract rose. The digestion of [Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest)'s evangelical segment, not the day's frictions, appears to have driven the movement.

## In summary

1. The [market](https://polymarket.com/event/brazil-presidential-election) consolidated Lula's favoritism (47.50%, USD 6.38M) and opened the widest gap of the cycle over Flávio (+21.00pp), digesting the religious segment of [Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest) from June 10.
2. Without a new national poll, the day's data was the [Quaest segment among evangelicals](https://www.cartacapital.com.br/cartaexpressa/as-intencoes-de-voto-para-presidente-entre-evangelicos-e-catolicos-segundo-a-quaest/) (Flávio −9pp, Lula +7pp), confirmed by multiple outlets; the calendar for the next 7 days is dominated by state-level surveys.
3. The widest divergence on the dashboard remains Renan (market 13.70% × survey 3%), although the market maintains him as the favorite for 3rd place in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno); the Master case lost momentum ([STF](/en/glossary#stf) impeachment stalled at 2.30%).
